title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 2 Lesson 2: Multi-Force Equilibrium Two Or More Unknowns custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle is held in equilibrium by four forces acting along the coordinate axes: a force of $25\text{ N}$ in the positive $x$-direction, a force of $18\text{ N}$ in the positive $y$-direction, a force of magnitude $P$ in the negative $x$-direction, and a force of magnitude $Q$ in the negative $y$-direction. State the values of $P$ and $Q$.

Two unknown forces of magnitudes $P$ and $Q$ act at angles of $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ above the positive and negative $x$-axes respectively. Together, they hold a particle in equilibrium against a downward vertical load of $40\text{ N}$, with no other forces acting. Determine the exact value of $P$ and calculate $Q$ correct to 3 significant figures.

A particle is in equilibrium under the action of four coplanar forces: $10\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis, $20\text{ N}$ along the positive $y$-axis, $30\text{ N}$ along the negative $x$-axis, and a fourth force $\mathbf{F}$. Calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf{F}$, and find the angle that $\mathbf{F}$ makes below the positive $x$-axis.

A particle of weight $W = 50\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two identical strings making angles of $45^\circ$ with the horizontal ceiling. By symmetry and resolution, determine the tension $T$ in each string.

Three coplanar forces of magnitudes $15\text{ N}$ along $+x$, $25\text{ N}$ along $+y$, and $35\text{ N}$ along $-x$ act on a particle. A fourth force $\mathbf{P}$ of magnitude $P$ holds the particle in equilibrium. Calculate the value of $P$ correct to 3 significant figures, and find the angle $\theta$ that $\mathbf{P}$ makes with the downward vertical.

A particle is held in equilibrium by four forces: an unknown horizontal force $P$ acting in the positive $x$-direction, an unknown vertical force $Q$ acting in the positive $y$-direction, a force of $40\text{ N}$ acting at $30^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis, and a force of $60\text{ N}$ acting at $60^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis. Calculate the values of $P$ and $Q$ correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 4\text{ kg}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings attached to a horizontal ceiling. String 1 makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the ceiling and carries tension $T_1$. String 2 makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the ceiling and carries tension $T_2$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces horizontally and vertically, form two simultaneous equations for the tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ in the two strings.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations to find the exact value of $T_1$, and calculate the value of $T_2$ correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
Four coplanar forces act at a point and maintain a particle in equilibrium:
- A force of $50\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis.
- A force of $60\text{ N}$ along the positive $y$-axis.
- A force of magnitude $P$ acting in the negative $x$-direction.
- A force of magnitude $Q$ acting at an angle of $30^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis (into the fourth quadrant).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces vertically in equilibrium, determine the magnitude of force $Q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces horizontally in equilibrium, determine the exact value of $P$ in surd form, and calculate its value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
Four coplanar forces act at a point $O$ and maintain a particle in equilibrium:
- Force $\mathbf{F}_1$ has magnitude $40\text{ N}$ and acts at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_2$ has magnitude $30\text{ N}$ and acts at an angle of $45^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_3$ has magnitude $15\text{ N}$ and acts along the negative $y$-axis.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_4$ has unknown magnitude $P$ and acts at an angle $\theta$ below the negative $x$-axis ($0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving horizontally and vertically in equilibrium, calculate the value of $P\cos\theta$ and the value of $P\sin\theta$, giving each value correct to 3 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Hence determine the angle $\theta$ correct to 1 decimal place, and calculate the magnitude $P$ correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of weight $W = 50\text{ N}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings $A$ and $B$, while being pushed to the right by a horizontal force of $10\text{ N}$. String $A$ is inclined at $40^\circ$ to the vertical and carries tension $T_A$. String $B$ is inclined at $50^\circ$ to the vertical and carries tension $T_B$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving horizontally and vertically in equilibrium, write down two linear simultaneous equations for the tensions $T_A$ and $T_B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations to determine the tension $T_A$ and the tension $T_B$, giving each value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 3\text{ kg}$ is held in equilibrium on a smooth inclined plane making an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal. The particle is acted on by two external forces: a horizontal force of magnitude $H$ directed into the plane, and a force of magnitude $F$ acting up the line of greatest slope of the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces parallel to the inclined plane, express $F$ in terms of $H$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that $H = 10\text{ N}$, calculate the exact value of $F$ in surd form, and give its value correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces perpendicular to the inclined plane, calculate the normal reaction $R_N$ exerted by the plane on the particle correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
Five coplanar forces act at a point $O$ and maintain a particle in equilibrium:
- Force $\mathbf{F}_1$ has magnitude $30\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_2$ has magnitude $40\text{ N}$ at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_3$ has magnitude $25\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$ at an angle of $45^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_4$ has unknown magnitude $P$ and acts in the negative $y$-direction.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_5$ has unknown magnitude $Q$ and acts at an angle of $30^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis (into the third quadrant).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces horizontally in equilibrium, determine the exact value of $Q$ in surd form, and calculate its value correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces vertically in equilibrium, determine the exact value of $P$ in surd form, and calculate its value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ is suspended at junction $O$ by two light inextensible strings $OA$ and $OB$ attached to fixed ceiling supports at the same horizontal level. A variable horizontal pulling force of magnitude $P$ acts on the particle to the right. String $OA$ makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the horizontal ceiling and carries tension $T_A$. String $OB$ makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal ceiling and carries tension $T_B$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces horizontally and vertically in equilibrium, express the tensions $T_A$ and $T_B$ in terms of $P$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine the value of $P$ for which $T_A = 2 T_B$, and calculate this value of $P$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum horizontal force $P_{\max}$ that can be applied to the right before string $OB$ becomes slack, and calculate the tension $T_A$ in this limiting state.
